cohort: Low-risk laboring mothers at Debre Markos Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Northwest Ethiopia
finding: Routine use of continuous EFM in low-risk laboring mothers was associated with increased rates of cesarean sections and instrumental vaginal deliveries compared to intermittent auscultation, without significant improvement in immediate newborn outcomes.
mod_finding: Continuous EFM was associated with higher rates of instrumental-assisted vaginal delivery (7% vs 2.4%) and cesarean sections (16% vs 2%) compared to intermittent auscultation.
